newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's secret police chief resigns.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's secret police chief resigns.

text.p: The head of Colombia's state security police resigned on Thursday, less than seven months after he was appointed to the post by President Ernesto Samper.

Administrative Security Department (DAS) chief Jaime Cabrera gave no specific reason for his decision to step down in a letter to Samper that was made public by the president's press office. But in a return letter accepting the resignation, Samper thanked him for having explained that it was due to other "professional commitments."

Cabrera, a 38-year-old former deputy justice minister, judge and university law professor, was named director of the DAS on June 25, 1996, after his predecessor, Marco Tulio Gutierrez, stepped down amid allegations that he had tapped U.S. Embassy telephone lines and spied on U.S. diplomats in Bogota.
Gutierrez also grabbed headlines, shortly before leaving public office, by calling for the expulsion of U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette.
